Barcelona must prove that they’ve learned the harsh lesson that Atleti inflicted on them last season. This is an important chance at redemption, and a chance to show they’ve truly turned a page.

item.title: Rayan Ait-Nouri: Man United receive positive update in January pursuit of Man City ace
item.description: Rayan Ait-Nouri: Man United receive positive update in January pursuit of Man City ace Manchester United secured a stunning 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma at Old Trafford in the Champions League. However, the game further highlighted a gap in the squad that has been hurting the Red Devils for some time. Diogo Dalot started at left-back in the absence of Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu, both of whom are sidelined with injuries. The Portuguese defender has covered in the position before but is not a natural solution for the role. Dalot was caught out of position for Roma’s first goal, with Matias Soule afforded time and space to send the visitors ahead. While that ultimately amounted to nothing thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha brace, United will look to address the issue in January. United failed to sign a left-back in the summer The Red Devils wanted to sign a new left-back this summer and among the candidates on their wish list was Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri. While INEOS failed to get a deal across the line, recent reports suggest that they are ready to return for the Algerian at the turn of the year. Ait-Nouri was a revelation for Wolverhampton Wanderers and moved to the Etihad in the summer of 2025. Unfortunately, he has struggled for game time with the Cityzens so far, and he could be tempted to leave in search of greener pastures in January. The 25-year-old has pace to burn, is attack-minded and knows the Premier League well. With also a point to prove after dropping down the pecking order at City, a move to Old Trafford could help him get his career back on track. A fresh update on the saga has now emerged, which could be music to the ears of the Red Devils faithful. R. Aït-Nouri Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 Personal terms not an issue for United move Journalist Florian Plettenberg has confirmed United’s interest in Ait-Nouri and insists that personal terms will not be a hindrance to the move. In a post shared on X, he wrote: “Rayan Aït-Nouri, one to watch in the winter transfer window.” “The 25 y/o left-back is open to leaving Manchester City. Understand Manchester United would like to sign him. Personal terms are not an issue.” However, Plettenberg warned that the Red Devils could struggle to convince their bitter rivals to let him go. He concluded: “The main issue is the relationship between the two Manchester clubs. Aït-Nouri’s market is currently being explored.” United and City have endured contrasting fortunes in the past decade, but their rivalry remains as intense as ever. The Cityzens may not be too keen to strengthen their archenemies, especially in the middle of the season. If the Red Devils find little luck in this pursuit, they could turn their attentions to Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, who is reportedly ready to leave Camp Nou in January. Recent reports suggest they also have their eyes on rising Rennes star Mahamadou Nagida. Why? ✅ United are reportedly eyeing a January move for Ait-Nouri. ✅ The Algerian

item.title: Brian Brobbey 2031 — A New Chapter In Red And White
item.description: As Sunderland fans, there’s little better than watching someone grow into the shirt. Brian Brobbey has already given us plenty to celebrate in his near-fifteen months on Wearside, and there are plenty of reasons to believe his story his just beginning. Tuesday’s announcement that our number nine has signed a new long-term contract, keeping him at the club until 2031, is a huge statement. Brobbey has become crucial to how Sunderland play, and this news, despite coming with the club at a low point, could act as both a catalyst to boost the fanbase and to inspire Brobbey to find his best form. Since arriving from Ajax on deadline day in 2025, Brobbey has brought a physical presence that many defenders have struggled to deal with, dominating Gabriel, William Saliba, Ruben Dias and of course Dan Burn during his time on Wearside. His first season saw him score seven Premier League goals as Sunderland exceeded expectations, securing Europa League football and announcing ourselves back in the Premier League — and there were plenty of memorable moments along the way. The winner at St James’ Park won’t be forgotten in a hurry, while his goals against Arsenal, Tottenham, Everton, Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and that assist at Stamford Bridge helped turn Sunderland’s Premier League return into something unheard of in these parts. If there was one afternoon that truly showed Brobbey’s potential, it was that hat-trick against Manchester City at the Etihad in September, with three goals against one of the strongest defences in the world, never mind the country. Each goal demonstrated a poacher’s instinct — similarly to his goals for Netherlands in the World Cup, both of which came from low crosses across the six-yard box. If we can keep creating these types of chances, Brobbey will continue to score and lead us to more positive results in the Premier League and on the continent this season. The Dutchman became the first Sunderland player to score a Premier League hat-trick since Jermain Defoe in 2016, and he also won the Premier League’s Player of the Matchweek award for his performance. This was a reminder that when it clicks and we create the chances, Brobbey can trouble any defence in the division. For Sunderland, this deal protects a key asset, increasing our bargaining power if a team were to come in for Brobbey in the next few transfer windows, as well as maximising our income in a worst-case scenario come the end of the season, but we won’t mention the ‘R’ word today. Brobbey also represents the type of player Sunderland are looking for and want to build around: ambitious, committed, physical and still developing. The first chapter has been a good one; let’s hope the next can be even better. To describe Brobbey’s new deal in just one word, we’ll leave that to the man himself…

item.title: Brundle unconvinced Ferrari can stop another Hamilton-Leclerc clash
item.description: Martin Brundle expects another flashpoint between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc , warning that any internal talks within Ferrari following their clash in Mexico are unlikely to prevent a repeat. Ferrari missed out on a potential 1-2 after both drivers ran wide at Turn 4, when Leclerc challenged Hamilton for the lead. Max Verstappen capitalised to take the victory, with Hamilton finishing in P2 and Leclerc in P4. Brundle expects Ferrari to address the clash internally before this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. However, he questioned whether any meeting would prevent a repeat situation between their two drivers. He told Sky Sports:"it doesn't look pretty for the team, it's like when Lando (Norris) ran into Oscar Piastri in Singapore in the sprint race, it doesn't look pretty for the team and you let 1,500 people down and that's just the car side. You let people down in your team, you are only the final link in the chain of your team but you are the one out there that's got to deliver in the heat of the moment. "So Ferrari will have to manage that somehow and they will sit down, we will go to Brazil, and they will say 'yes we've sat down and we understood it all, move forward, it won't happen again,' but in reality we know that it will. Brundle: Leclerc has had frustrations this year Brundle also told Sky Sports that there has been some frustration within the Ferrari camp this season, particularly on Leclerc's side. After dominating Hamilton in 2025, Leclerc, until now, has been outperformed more often than not by the seven-time world champion. Despite Hamilton's criticism of Leclerc after the Mexico City Grand Prix, Brundle defended Leclerc, with a reference to Ayrton Senna's famous quote about not going for a gap which is there. He said: "You know what? They’re hardwired racing drivers. It’s a curious business we have where you perform as an individual totally in a team environment. You’re measured as an individual, you’re rewarded as an individual. “And then when the adrenaline’s up and the chance of the gap is there, as the great Ayrton Senna said, ‘If you don’t go for a gap, you’re no longer a racing driver.’ And that’s what they did. There’s some frustration. Charles had some frustrations this year."

item.title: Fan Letters: ‘We Need To Get Behind The Manager And The Lads’
item.description: Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris watches the Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Dear Roker Report We need to get behind the manager and the Lads. We’ve seen what constant change looks like, and it hasn’t exactly been a roaring success. New managers, new philosophies, rebuilding the squad every 12 months. At some point, you have to trust the process and give people time to develop. We’ve spent years demanding a long-term plan, but some supporters seem unwilling to tolerate the patience required to make one work. Getting Brobbey and Ballard back are big steps in the right direction. Injuries and a harsh hand from the fixture computer have contributed to the position we sit in the table. Yes, the players and the manager could also do better, but something positive is just around the corner. Let’s not end up like the shower up the road, who boo their team off the park at half-time and full-time. We’re better than that. Steve, Washington Editor’s note [Martin] Thanks for the email Steve. We’ve all seen what happens when we don’t have stability – no one wants to go back to those days. Similarly, I’m sure the vast majority of us want Regis Le Bris to enjoy more and more success here. Change doesn’t automatically mean things are going to go well – nor does it mean they’re going to go badly. Le Bris staying doesn’t guarantee either of those either. We can all see where we need to improve, and the reality is the players’ performance hasn’t been good enough this season, and neither have results. The ideal is Le Bris is able to change that – the question is how long can the club wait for things to change? I believe the playing squad is more than capable of competing towards the top third of the league, and I suspect the club believe that too. So putting sentiment and the past to one side, he needs to start getting results over the next couple of months, or he’ll be replaced. Dear Roker Report I think Sunderland supporters should give credit where it’s due for what Régis has done over the three years he’s been with us. After all, look how long it took Sir Alex Ferguson to get there when he was manager. So come on, supporters, give Régis a chance. He’s the best manager we’ve had in years. Ian Frame Editor’s note [Martin] Thanks for the email Ian. I don’t think anyone would fail to give Le Bris credit for what he’s achieved in the 2 seasons he’s had here. Hopefully he’ll turn this situation around – however if a new manager had come in in the summer and the team was producing this level of performance and results he’d likely already have gone. Football moves quickly, it’s a results business, you know the cliches, and if things don’t drastically pick up soon we’ll be in massive trouble. The Ferguson example is relevant, albeit in a different era. But I bet there aren’t many Man Utd fans who i
item.content:encoded: Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris watches the Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Dear Roker Report We need to get behind the manager and the Lads. We’ve seen what constant change looks like, and it hasn’t exactly been a roaring success. New managers, new philosophies, rebuilding the squad every 12 months. At some point, you have to trust the process and give people time to develop. We’ve spent years demanding a long-term plan, but some supporters seem unwilling to tolerate the patience required to make one work. Getting Brobbey and Ballard back are big steps in the right direction. Injuries and a harsh hand from the fixture computer have contributed to the position we sit in the table. Yes, the players and the manager could also do better, but something positive is just around the corner. Let’s not end up like the shower up the road, who boo their team off the park at half-time and full-time. We’re better than that. Steve, Washington Editor’s note [Martin] Thanks for the email Steve. We’ve all seen what happens when we don’t have stability – no one wants to go back to those days. Similarly, I’m sure the vast majority of us want Regis Le Bris to enjoy more and more success here. Change doesn’t automatically mean things are going to go well – nor does it mean they’re going to go badly. Le Bris staying doesn’t guarantee either of those either. We can all see where we need to improve, and the reality is the players’ performance hasn’t been good enough this season, and neither have results. The ideal is Le Bris is able to change that – the question is how long can the club wait for things to change? I believe the playing squad is more than capable of competing towards the top third of the league, and I suspect the club believe that too. So putting sentiment and the past to one side, he needs to start getting results over the next couple of months, or he’ll be replaced. Dear Roker Report I think Sunderland supporters should give credit where it’s due for what Régis has done over the three years he’s been with us. After all, look how long it took Sir Alex Ferguson to get there when he was manager. So come on, supporters, give Régis a chance. He’s the best manager we’ve had in years. Ian Frame Editor’s note [Martin] Thanks for the email Ian. I don’t think anyone would fail to give Le Bris credit for what he’s achieved in the 2 seasons he’s had here. Hopefully he’ll turn this situation around – however if a new manager had come in in the summer and the team was producing this level of performance and results he’d likely already have gone. Football moves quickly, it’s a results business, you know the cliches, and if things don’t drastically pick up soon we’ll be in massive trouble. The Ferguson example is relevant, albeit in a different era. But I bet there aren’t many Man Utd fans who in hindsight say ‘‘we should have kept big Ron”. Sometime change is necessary. I’m hoping Le Bris turns this round, I genuinely am, but he needs results, quickly.

item.title: What’s The Root Cause Of Sunderland’s Current Struggles?
item.description: Regis Le Bris, manager of Sunderland AFC, looks on during the Carabao Cup Round of 16 match between Sunderland and Brentford at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images As we sit looking up at the rest of the table, it’s fair to ask why. Success again, and we collected an unexpected bonus in Thomas Meunier. ​The recruitment team succeeded with the acquisition of a left winger but failed to secure someone to operate on the right. I’m not going to criticise the failure to find someone ready to play an understudy role to Brian Brobbey, as that was always a big ask. We brought in one for the future in Juan Angulo and realistically, that’s all we could expect. ​So, ultimately we failed with the right winger, that’s all. item.content:encoded: Regis Le Bris, manager of Sunderland AFC, looks on during the Carabao Cup Round of 16 match between Sunderland and Brentford at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images As we sit looking up at the rest of the table, it’s fair to ask why. Either the recruitment has failed, or the coach is at fault. If the players lack confidence, make basic errors or are simply out of form, it’s the coach’s job to correct it. ​Starting with recruitment, let’s look back at the summer’s business. Most supporters seemed to agree on what we needed: a left back, cover for Granit Xhaka, a right and left winger, a third forward and possibly a centre half. ​Left back and Xhaka’s backup? Check, and it looks like we have a real find on our hands with Jules Ahoka. A central defender? Success again, and we collected an unexpected bonus in Thomas Meunier. ​The recruitment team succeeded with the acquisition of a left winger but failed to secure someone to operate on the right. I’m not going to criticise the failure to find someone ready to play an understudy role to Brian Brobbey, as that was always a big ask. We brought in one for the future in Juan Angulo and realistically, that’s all we could expect. ​So, ultimately we failed with the right winger, that’s all. The key question is: would Regis Le Bris have played with two wingers if they were available? I have my doubts. ​A quick review of our ten most expensive signings shows four of them are wingers (Malick Fofana, Simon Adingra, Nilson Angulo and Chemesdine Talbi). All are still on the club’s books, with Talbi recording the most Premier League starts with twenty to date. Adingra (ten starts) has been shipped out on loan and there’s obviously an issue with Talbi. This leaves Angulo (sixteen starts) as the only one consistently getting a game, as Fofana has hardly featured in the league. ​Some might point to inexperience, but the evidence shows otherwise. Around 30% of current Premier League footballers are under twenty three, so age is not the issue. Angulo appears to be the current favourite for the left-wing role but is the most inexperienced. ​Adingra had over sixty Premier League appearances and was an Ivory Coast international when he joined Sunderland. Talbi was less experienced but a Moroccan international with thirty appearances in the Belgian Pro League. Fofana had made over fifty appearances in Ligue 1 and a further fifty in the Belgian Pro League to his name when he was recruited. ​Four wingers at a combined cost of £92 million, with one a regular starter and the rest bit-part players, is not a good return. Nine games in, Fofana is still not a regular starter, and his situation has finally convinced me the ongoing problem with our wingers isn’t recruitment — it’s the coach. ​It’s true that Fofana has been asked to rapidly bed in with a new team and get used to a radically different league, but I’m sorry, that’s the nature of the beast. On a human level, football is a brutal game and whatever the circumstances, players have to step up and perform. It’s that simple. ​Arsenal were apparently interested in Fofana’s services. Crystal Palace certainly were, so what’s happened and why is it not working? Sorry, but that’s down to the coaching and/or tactics. Again, I’m being harsh but I suspect Régis Le Bris’ current tactics would make Jeremy Doku look average. ​Now to midfield — the nub of the issue. Xhaka has been poor and that in turn has dragged down the performance levels of Noah Sadiki in particular, but also Enzo Le Fée. I am going to given the recruitment some criticism here and suggest they should have been ready for that possibility given Xhaka’s age and the impact of the Chelsea nonsense. They should have had a ready-to-go replacement. That said, Ahoka should be getting more game time, and that’s down to the coach. ​Finally, there is the defence, and I don’t believe there’s been a failure of recruitment there. We have five proven central defenders and one (Meunier) who could play there if needed. It’s true one centre half has a relatively long-term injury and two are badly out of form, but how many centre halves are we expected to carry in the squad? Is poor form down to the recruitment or the coach? ​Some might claim we lack flair players, but I disagree. First, as evidence to the court, I present Le Fée — enough said. I’ve already covered the winger situation, but to compound the baffling Talbi exclusion, he’s shown that he can be a threat when used as an attacking ten, and Chris Rigg could be a lot more expansive if given the opportunity. ​Habib Diarra would be classed as a ‘flair player’ if he could play more than five minutes without breaking down. As our most expensive player, I assume the coach had a significant input into his signing, so if he were available, where would he play? ​We’ll have to wait and see what happens if Diarra is available for an extended period, but currently I don’t see Le Bris using him in the free-flowing attacking role that plays to his strengths. ​For example, I suggest Diarra could play as an attacking ten. He could be a Kevin Phillips-type ten, playing off a big man (not quite as tall as Niall Quinn but about twice as wide). It would mean moving Le Fée but it would be an option, and Talbi could even fill that role as a backup. ​Can I see Le Bris considering such an admittedly radical option, or any other option that diverges significantly from the current team structure? No, and that’s a problem. Something needs to change because if he persists with the current approach, it’s not going to end well. ​To be fair to the recruitment team, the options are there but most involve more than minor tweaks. Can Le Bris find the answers? I really hope so, and he certainly deserves the backing to try.

item.title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Rangers’ Win Over Blues
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The New York Rangers secured a 3-1 win over the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night, snapping a four-game losing streak in the process. Here are some of the main takeaways from the Rangers’ victory: Dylan Garand Bounces Back: Leading into Tuesday night, Garand had started eight of the Rangers’ nine games in the wake of Igor Shesterkin’s season-ending injury, and the cracks in his game were beginning to show as his workload continued to mount and fatigue set in. After the team’s 4-1 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Sunday night, Garand was critical of himself, putting the blame solely on his shoulders. “Honestly, inexcusable,” Garand said of his performance on Sunday night. “Let the guys down. Pretty disappointing, put that loss on me. And yeah, it sucks.” The 24-year-old goaltender bounced back in a big way against the Blues, making 32 saves on 33 shots. Over the course of the night, Garand made some timely stops whenever the Blues gained offensive momentum, and he appeared to be steadier and more composed in his crease. “I just felt good,” Garand said. “I just really tried not to think out there. I think I've been doing too much of that lately in my game, so I just tried to go out there and battle and stop pucks.” Going into the night, Garand was facing scrutiny, with his game beginning to go in the wrong direction after a strong start to the season. However, his near-shutout performance helped keep the Rangers afloat throughout the contest and ultimately helped propel them to a much-needed victory. Mike Sullivan has been most impressed with Garand’s mental toughness and resilience through difficult times. “I think this game was an important one for him,” Sullivan said of Garand. “He wanted to bounce back and have a solid night for the group, and he did. I think his resilience, just his ability to move by circumstances and not not let it affect his performance or his game moving forward… I think that's a maturity that I've certainly witnessed in the short time that I've been around him. I think he’s proven what he’s capable of.” Will Cuylle Thrives At Center: Sullivan decided to tweak his lines going into Tuesday night’s matchup, with the biggest change revolving around putting Cuylle at the center position. Cuylle had never played center at any level of hockey, but Sullivan believed his skills translated well to playing down the middle. “I just feel like where we're at, we need to affect a little bit of change,” Sullivan said. “Will has a lot of qualities or the attributes that I think would allow him to be effective at that position. item.content:encoded: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The New York Rangers secured a 3-1 win over the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night, snapping a four-game losing streak in the process. Here are some of the main takeaways from the Rangers’ victory: Dylan Garand Bounces Back: Leading into Tuesday night, Garand had started eight of the Rangers’ nine games in the wake of Igor Shesterkin’s season-ending injury, and the cracks in his game were beginning to show as his workload continued to mount and fatigue set in. After the team’s 4-1 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Sunday night, Garand was critical of himself, putting the blame solely on his shoulders. “Honestly, inexcusable,” Garand said of his performance on Sunday night. “Let the guys down. Pretty disappointing, put that loss on me. And yeah, it sucks.” The 24-year-old goaltender bounced back in a big way against the Blues, making 32 saves on 33 shots. Over the course of the night, Garand made some timely stops whenever the Blues gained offensive momentum, and he appeared to be steadier and more composed in his crease. “I just felt good,” Garand said. “I just really tried not to think out there. I think I've been doing too much of that lately in my game, so I just tried to go out there and battle and stop pucks.” Going into the night, Garand was facing scrutiny, with his game beginning to go in the wrong direction after a strong start to the season. However, his near-shutout performance helped keep the Rangers afloat throughout the contest and ultimately helped propel them to a much-needed victory. Mike Sullivan has been most impressed with Garand’s mental toughness and resilience through difficult times. “I think this game was an important one for him,” Sullivan said of Garand. “He wanted to bounce back and have a solid night for the group, and he did. I think his resilience, just his ability to move by circumstances and not not let it affect his performance or his game moving forward… I think that's a maturity that I've certainly witnessed in the short time that I've been around him. I think he’s proven what he’s capable of.” Will Cuylle Thrives At Center: Sullivan decided to tweak his lines going into Tuesday night’s matchup, with the biggest change revolving around putting Cuylle at the center position. Cuylle had never played center at any level of hockey, but Sullivan believed his skills translated well to playing down the middle. “I just feel like where we're at, we need to affect a little bit of change,” Sullivan said. “Will has a lot of qualities or the attributes that I think would allow him to be effective at that position. He can skate, he has good size, he can lean on people down low.” Anchoring the Rangers’ third line alongside Oliver Bjorkstrand and Eeli Tolvanen, Cuylle looked natural at center while continuing to play the same physical, hard-forechecking game we’ve grown accustomed to seeing from him. “I was excited before the game,” Cuylle said. “Obviously, a challenge for me, something I've never done. Kind of felt a little nervous before the game, but after first couple shifts, settled in and just felt like myself.” Cuylle created an offensive-zone turnover in the third period, which helped lead to a goal from Bjorkstrand, giving the Rangers a 2-0 lead. Playing on both the power play and penalty kill, Cuylle logged a total of 18:19, the third-most among all Rangers forwards. The switch to center, on top of his usage in critical situations, shows Sullivan’s evolving trust in Cuylle as he continues to develop his game. “I thought he played real well. I thought he had a comfort level there. I liked what I saw,” Sullivan said of Cuylle’s performance playing center. Rangers' New-Look Fourth Line Provides Energy: The Blueshirts came into this game with quite a few line changes, including forming a new-look fourth line featuring Jaroslav Chmelař, Noah Laba, and Matt Rempe. All three players had a lot to prove. Chmelař was called up from the Hartford Wolf Pack of the American Hockey League just one day before, hungry to etch his mark in the NHL. Laba was moved down to the fourth line after Sullivan called his overall game a “mixed bag,” and Rempe had only been in the lineup for two of the Rangers’ previous 15 games. The newly assembled trio provided the Rangers with energy that the team has not gotten from its fourth line for much of the season. They were able to spend a large chunk of their shifts in the offensive zone, generating offense in the process while using their physicality well at both ends of the ice. “I thought they had a really solid game for us,” Sullivan said of the fourth line. “Labs and Jaro can really skate. I think they add a lot of pace to that line, and Remps obviously with his size and his reach and his and his aggressiveness. “I thought they had some really good momentum shifts for us. They spent a significant amount of time in the offensive zone. They had a couple of scoring opportunities, but the biggest thing that that line can bring to the team I think is just helping us create momentum with their physical play.” Since Joe Veleno went down with a lower-body injury, Sullivan has kept his fourth line on a short leash. However, he seemed to find a rhythm on Tuesday night, deploying the fourth line more frequently, with both Chmelař and Rempe playing over eight minutes despite not seeing any time on special teams. Scott Morrow Showing Improvement: Despite making the Rangers’ opening-night roster out of training camp, Scott Morrow served as a healthy scratch over the team’s first 14 games of the season. “I wouldn’t call it difficult necessarily,” Morrow said on not playing at all to start the season. “I feel blessed to be here, be a part of this group. Just trying to stay ready, have a positive attitude, and be ready for my chance to play.” A lower-body injury to Sean Durzi has given Morrow a chance to step into the lineup, and he’s been able to seize this opportunity. In two games, the 24-year-old defenseman has continued to flash his impressive puckhandling abilities, quick skating, and offensive instincts, skills we already knew were in his wheelhouse. However, what’s been a surprise is his improved defensive play. Morrow struggled to defend at a consistent level last year, one of the biggest reasons he spent a large chunk of the 2025-26 season playing in the American Hockey League. However, he’s shown heightened awareness from a defensive standpoint over this short two-game sample size. “Scotty has played well,” Sullivan said. “I think his pace is better. I think he's quicker. He's closing on people. I think his stick detail, just disrupting plays, getting his stick on the puck, things of that nature. I think that continues to evolve and improve and get better. I think he's making pretty good reads defensively. I know Scotty is making a real concerted effort on the defensive side of the puck to try to continue to evolve and improve.”

item.title: Rams QB Matthew Stafford’s wife rips NFL on Instagram for bye week schedule quirk
item.description: Rams QB Matthew Stafford’s wife rips NFL on Instagram for bye week schedule quirk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams have a relatively short bye week coming up, a scheduling decision that hasn’t sat well with quarterback Matthew Stafford ’s wife, Kelly, who made her displeasure with the NFL public. In an Instagram Story posted on Tuesday, Kelly tagged the league’s official account and questioned why Los Angeles is the only team without a traditional bye week , seeking an explanation for the shortened break. “Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week,” wrote Kelly. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) She also brought some humor into her criticism, pointing out that even after spending 18 years around professional football, she needs a break despite never having played a snap. “Because after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap. I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.” Moreover, Kelly invited the NFL to respond about its scheduling decision by adding a question box. The Rams technically have a Week 11 bye, but their schedule gives them considerably less time away from competition than a conventional midseason break. Los Angeles will face the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, November 15, before returning to the field against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25. The matchup will be the league’s first Thanksgiving Eve game and will be played at SoFi Stadium, with Netflix carrying the broadcast. Instead of receiving the usual two-week gap between games, the Rams will have just 10 days between their Cardinals and Packers matchups. Green Bay, meanwhile, will have a more favorable arrangement after the Thanksgiving Eve contest. The team will immediately enter its bye week and will not play again until December 6. Los Angeles’ demanding schedule extends beyond its shortened break. The Rams are projected to travel 34,847 miles during the season, making them the NFL’s second-most-traveled team behind the San Francisco 49ers, who are scheduled to cover 38,105 miles. Both NFC West rivals opened their campaigns in Melbourne, Australia, on September 10. The Rams have several challenging matchups remaining. Following their Packers game, they will have eight days before facing the Kansas City Chiefs on December 3. Their remaining schedule includes games against the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before a season-ending home matchup versus the Seahawks. Related: Rams HC Sean McVay provides key Myles Garrett injury update before Commanders clash Related: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns

item.title: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals
item.description: MACKINAW CITY — Mackinaw City will play for an MHSAA Division 4 district volleyball title . Taking on Mackinac Island in a district semifinal , the Comets booked their ticket to a championship clash at St. Ignace by capturing a 3-0 victory (25-12, 25-11, 25-16) over the Lakers in Mackinaw City on Tuesday, Nov. 3. MACK CITY'S RIAN ESPER: Esper a key Mackinaw City volleyball player in many different spots MACK CITY BOYS QUALIFY FOR XC STATES: Area's top performers paced by state-qualifier Mackinaw City boys XC DISTRICT VOLLEYBALL PREVIEW: Previewing, predicting Cheboygan-area volleyball district tournaments After starting slow and trailing 7-1 in the first set, the Comets (13-22-5) regrouped, battled back and took a one-set lead in the match. From there, they were in cruise control behind quality offensive and defensive play. "Once we were able to get ourselves settled, we played some very solid volleyball tonight and did a great job of getting into our system offensively, and our defense did a great job of digging balls and keeping balls alive to give ourselves a shot at winning some long volleys," Mackinaw City coach Jake Huffman said. Rian Esper's 10 kills, six aces and six digs fueled the Comets, who received 16 assists, seven digs, two kills and seven digs from Julia Short, and 11 digs, six assists, four kills and three aces from Emily Kruczynski. Mackinaw City's many other contributors included Alaia Mendez (eight kills, five aces, four digs), Poppy Wallace (five kills, two digs, one block), Ella Kruczynski (six aces, five digs, one assist), and Sarah Lentell (two kills, one dig). "I was very happy with our response and proud of the effort that ladies put forth tonight," Huffman said. "We will use (Wednesday) to prep for a very tough St. Ignace squad on Thursday." Thursday's district final at St. Ignace (10-11-7) is a 6 p.m. start. Eagles beat Alanson, will meet Harbor Light for title HARBOR SPRINGS — Get ready for a Northern Lakes Conference showdown for the district title on Thursday. Opening its postseason in style was the Burt Lake Northern Michigan Christian Academy volleyball team, which earned a 3-0 victory over Alanson (25-17, 25-10, 25-15) in an MHSAA Division 4 semifinal at Harbor Light on Tuesday, Nov. 3. The Eagles (23-6-2) were led by Shanna Ferraiuolo, who finished with 21 kills and four digs, while Lauren Ferraiuolo tallied 18 kills, three aces and three digs, and Hazel Bowman added 38 assists and three aces. Isabel Hoffmeyer chipped in with 12 digs. "Always nice to get a postseason win," NMCA coach Josh Ferraiuolo said. "We were a little rusty after being off for more than a week, but overall, we played pretty well. Looking forward to a very competitive final on Thursday." NMCA faces Harbor Light (16-6-6) in a 6 p.m. final on Thursday, Nov. 5, at Harbor Light. Harbor Light defeated Pellston 3-0 (25-14, 25-16, 25-7) in a semifinal on Tuesday. The Eagles (23-6-2) were led by Shanna Ferraiuolo, who finished with 21 kills and four digs, while Lauren Ferraiuolo tallied 18 kills, three aces and three digs, and Hazel Bowman added 38 assists and three aces. Isabel Hoffmeyer chipped in with 12 digs. "Always nice to get a postseason win," NMCA coach Josh Ferraiuolo said. "We were a little rusty after being off for more than a week, but overall, we played pretty well. Looking forward to a very competitive final on Thursday." NMCA faces Harbor Light (16-6-6) in a 6 p.m. final on Thursday, Nov. 5, at Harbor Light. Harbor Light defeated Pellston 3-0 (25-14, 25-16, 25-7) in a semifinal on Tuesday. Inland Lakes falls to Harbor Springs in 3 CHARLEVOIX — The Inland Lakes volleyball team's season ended following a 3-0 loss to Harbor Springs (22-25, 23-25, 24-26) in an MHSAA Division 3 district first-round match in Charlevoix on Monday, Nov. 2. "The girls battled hard all night, we had great contributions from every player on the team. Unfortunately, we just struggled putting the ball away in those high-pressure situations, and Harbor capitalized on that," Inland Lakes coach Shaylee Michael said. VOTE FOR ATHLETE OF THE WEEK: Vote! Who should be Daily Tribune's Athlete of the Week, Oct. 26-31? XC STATE QUALIFIERS: Meet the Cheboygan area's 2026 MHSAA cross country state qualifiers Ava Belford finished with 11 kills, six digs and one ace to lead the Bulldogs (10-21-4), while Adisyn Fenstermaker tallied 11 digs, three kills and two aces, Mariah King had 22 assists, 10 digs, four kills and one ace, Emmalynn Connelly added seven kills, one ace and one block, and Khali Woollard collected 12 digs and one ace. "This team has made immense progress from the beginning of the season to now, and I am very proud of the work they have put in," Michael said. item.title: Caitlin Clark’s latest heartwarming gesture sees her send a massive gift to her alma mater
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release. Clark dominated the NCAA with a four-year stint with the Hawkeyes. Although she never won a national championship, losing in the 2023 and 2024 finals, she set countless records for the college and the NCAA as a whole. Now with her third WNBA season in the rearview, Clark showed love to where she became a national superstar by sending a gift over to the current women’s basketball team on the Hawkeyes. Caitlin Clark gifts CC1s to Iowa Hawkeyes women’s basketball team Clark sent over custom black-and-gold Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes to the Hawkeyes, creating a player-exclusive Iowa PE colorway for their season-opener against Towson. The team shared a video of the excited reactions current players had to the gift. The Hawkeyes also shared an in-game picture of how the sneakers looked on the players’ feet during the game. While Clark has previously gifted sneakers to the Hawkeyes team, including pairs of the CC1s, this is the first time she has created a team-exclusive PE for the players, featuring the University of Iowa Tigerhawk logo on the tongue. The Hawkeyes picked up a convincing 73-45 win over the Towson Tigers in their CBB season-opener on November 3. Junior Dani Carnegie, who was a freshman during Clark’s final year with the Hawkeyes, led them to the win with 21 points, five rebounds and five assists. Clark left the Hawkeyes without a championship, but set the NCAA Division 1 basketball scoring record with 2,951 points, breaking Pete Maravich’s 54-year-old 3,667-point record. She has also made the most three-pointers in NCAA history with 548, with her 201 threes in 23-24 setting the record for most in one season. Her legacy as a Hawkeye is arguably richer than any current professional athlete due to the historic nature of her four-year tenure. While not having a championship to cement it as the greatest NCAA career of all time is rough, she gave Iowa years of incredible basketball. Read more: What Caitlin Clark does that makes the rest of the WNBA ‘mad’ ‘Insane’ – Sophie Cunningham reacts to adults dressing as her for Halloween Caitlin Clark picks what was ‘the best part’ about the WNBA Finals series

item.title: Vikings’ Carson Wentz Gets Good News on Promotion Before Bills Game
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz. Getty The Minnesota Vikings won again in Week 7 arguably despite quarterback Kyler Murray. Getty The Vikings set Carson Wentz up for a big payday, but there is some strong doubts he will cash in. Getty Calls among Minnesota Vikings fans and media members who cover the team regularly are steadily growing for Kevin O’Connell to make a change under center from Kyler Murray to Carson Wentz, and the head coach may have just caught the break he needed to do so while still allowing the franchise to save face. The Vikings named Murray the starting QB over JJ McCarthy before either had taken a preseason snap. Minnesota then demoted McCarthy to QB3 before trading him to the New York Giants for a fifth-round draft asset in what was a fairly historic punt on top-10 pick in just his third NFL season at 23 years old and with only 10 starts on his resumé. Murray has not performed poorly enough that one can accurately call his season through seven games a worst-case scenario for the Vikings. But across the range of possible outcomes, Murray has definitely produced on the lower end of the spectrum. Benching him outright now would equate to O’Connell and first-year GM Nolan Teasley admitting that Murray’s elevation to QB1 and the team’s hastiness to sell low on McCarthy were both significant mistakes. However, Murray’s moderate hamstring concern, which he suffered in the team’s first loss of the season last week to the Detroit Lions , might be precisely the window O’Connell requires to go back to Wentz while maintaining plausible deniability with regards to Murray. Kyler Murray Suffered Hamstring Concern Last Week Getty Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray. O’Connell mentioned during the postgame that hamstring tightness was the reason for Murray’s trip to the blue tent on the sidelines during the fourth quarter in Detroit. On Tuesday, November 3, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reported that Murray could miss time due to the injury, which isn’t overly severe but may impact his ability to scramble. “I don’t get the sense it’s really bad, but he is a mobile QB,” Rapoport said . “If he can’t move like he needs to, then I don’t know that he’s gonna play.” Making plays with his legs has been Murray’s saving grace this season, and if he can’t do that effectively, it’s hard to imagine the Vikings scoring enough points to keep up with the visiting Buffalo Bills on next week’s addition of “Monday Night Football.” Vikings Arguably Soft-Benched JJ McCarthy for Carson Wentz Last Season Getty Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk wrote Tuesday that he suspects the Vikings will use Murray’s injury as “cover” for a “soft benching” that will allow O’Connell to go back to Wentz without formally demoting Murray. “It’s hard not to look at the current status of Murray’s hamstring ‘tightness’ as cover for a soft benching of Murray,” Florio wrote . “That gives the Vikings a chance to let Cars

Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk wrote Tuesday that he suspects the Vikings will use Murray’s injury as “cover” for a “soft benching” that will allow O’Connell to go back to Wentz without formally demoting Murray. “It’s hard not to look at the current status of Murray’s hamstring ‘tightness’ as cover for a soft benching of Murray,” Florio wrote . “That gives the Vikings a chance to let Carson Wentz, who played well enough in most of the Week 1 win over the Packers and all of the Week 2 win over the Bears .” Several analysts suggested that Minnesota did essentially the same thing last season after McCarthy suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 2. Wentz stepped in, starting the next five games over a six-week span that included the Vikings’ bye. McCarthy eventually got the starting job back, though only after Wentz went down for the season with a shoulder injury that required surgery. If he had not suffered that injury when he did, circumstances would have forced the Vikings to tip their hand as to their true preferences at QB, with six weeks being the upward amount of time any player might legitimately miss with an ankle sprain — absent any setbacks. item.title: Kentucky Gets Major Boost From Iowa State Transfer in Season Debut
item.description: LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - NOVEMBER 03: Milan Momcilovic #22 of the Kentucky Wildcats reacts during the second half against the Manhattan Jaspers at Rupp Arena on November 03, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - NOVEMBER 03: Milan Momcilovic #22 of the Kentucky Wildcats takes a shot over Ben Tweedy #6 of the Manhattan Jaspers during the second half at Rupp Arena on November 03, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - MARCH 13: forward Milan Momcilovic #22 of the Iowa State Cyclones shoots against the Arizona Wildcats in the first half during the semifinals of the Big 12 Tournament at T-Mobile Center on March 13, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images) Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - NOVEMBER 03: Milan Momcilovic #22 of the Kentucky Wildcats reacts after making a shot in front of Isaac Johnson #2 of the Manhattan Jaspers during the second half at Rupp Arena on November 03, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty Kentucky forward Milan Momcilovic impressed in his first game as a Wildcat. Momcilovic scored a game-high 24 points in Kentucky’s 85-57 win over Manhattan. The Iowa State transfer knocked down six of his nine three-point attempts. The Kentucky Forward was Efficient Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY – NOVEMBER 03: Milan Momcilovic #22 of the Kentucky Wildcats takes a shot over Ben Tweedy #6 of the Manhattan Jaspers during the second half at Rupp Arena on November 03, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Momcilovic made eight of his 12 shot attempts from the field and shot 66.7% from three. This allowed him to get a very efficient 24 points in 28 minutes of playing time. He looked very confident out there and worked perfectly for this Wildcat offense. Momcilovic didn’t get his first points until 7:21 left in the first half, when he knocked down a three. After he made that three, he was on fire, letting the game come to him. All it took for him to get going was to see the ball go through once, and he started hitting everything. Momcilovic’s Past Getty KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI – MARCH 13: forward Milan Momcilovic #22 of the Iowa State Cyclones shoots against the Arizona Wildcats in the first half during the semifinals of the Big 12 Tournament at T-Mobile Center on March 13, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images) At Iowa State, Momcilovic averaged 16.9 points and shot 48.7% from three, which is unbelievably good. That alone made him a big target for Kentucky to go out and try to get him. A good three-point shooter is what the Wildcats have needed, but instead they got a great three-point shooter. Momcilovic also earned second-team All-Big 12 honors. Kentucky brought him in so he could provide elite three-point shooting, and in one game, it looks like it’s already paying off. He did what the Wildcats’ offense needed him to do

item.title: Bulls Reportedly Open to Trading All-Star as Deadline Approaches
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Bryson Graham and head coach Tiago Splitter of the Chicago Bulls speak to the media during Chicago Bulls Media Day at the United Center on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Norman Powell #24 of the Chicago Bulls poses for a photo during Chicago Bulls Media Day at the United Center on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bulls could have a decision to make involving one of their offseason additions. According to NBA insider Jake Fischer, Chicago is looking to field offers for Norman Powell ahead of the trade deadline. The report puts a scorer into a conversation about how the Bulls intend to build their future. For fans, the development raises a question beyond whether Powell can help another team. Chicago added him to strengthen its offense and provide experience around younger players. Listening to offers would require weighing those benefits against whatever another organization might offer. Jake Fischer Reports Bulls’ Interest in Norman Powell Offers Fischer’s reported update concerns Chicago’s willingness to consider offers. It does not establish that a trade has been agreed upon or identify a confirmed destination. That distinction matters because availability alone does not determine a player’s return. Other teams must evaluate fit, salary and the assets they would need to surrender. Chicago would then have to decide whether the package improves its position enough to justify losing Powell. Powell joined the Bulls after earning his first All-Star selection with Miami last season. His agreement includes a team option for the second season, giving Chicago a future decision beyond the trade market. That structure leaves the organization multiple paths to consider. Additional perimeter scoring can help a team when its primary options face extra defensive attention. Powell’s experience could make him attractive to an organization seeking immediate offensive support rather than another developmental project. What a Powell Trade Could Mean for Chicago For the Bulls, however, moving a veteran should involve more than making room. Younger players benefit from opportunities, but they also need functional lineups and experienced teammates. Chicago must assess whether a deal supplies value without making development harder elsewhere. Keeping Powell carries its own argument. A reliable scoring presence can reduce the pressure on less experienced players and help an offense survive difficult stretches. Those contributions deserve consideration alongside draft picks or younger players that might appear in hypothetical offers. The decision ultimately comes down to what becomes available. A strong proposal could give Chicago a reason to adjust its plans. A disappointing market could make retaining Powell the more sensible choice. Fischer’s report makes Powell a name to monitor, not a player already departing. Bulls fans should watch the offers and reporting before judging the outcome. item.title: Lions Sign Ex-Cardinals Draft Pick After Jack Campbell Injury
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images Getty Jack Campbell of the Detroit Lions Getty The Detroit Lions have acted quickly in finding their replacement options for the injured Jack Campbell. First, the team signed K.J. Britt to their active roster. Their second move was signing linebacker Owen Pappoe to their practice squad. With Pappoe in the mix, it looks like the Lions have made their moves to replace Campbell and rookie Jimmy Rolder in the short term. Detroit Lions Sign Owen Pappoe to Practice Squad in Response to Jack Campbell Injury Getty Jack Campbell of the Detroit Lions The team lost two players from their active roster and signed Britt and Pappoe. Britt is on the active roster, as they signed him from the New England Patriots practice squad. However, Pappoe will join Joe Bachie on the practice squad with the Lions. Bachie is the likely name to get called up, as he has been with the team throughout the year, and he can provide help on special teams. With Britt up and Bachie expected to be called up, they have two replacements on the roster. Then, Pappoe would step in and replace Bachie. Detroit is likely going to try to start Malcolm Rodriguez next to Derrick Barnes as their starter. Trevor Nowaske will slide in as the third linebacker. Then, Amen Ogbongbemiga, Britt, and Bachie will serve as the backups. All three have special teams value, giving them a reason to be active. Still, the moves likely do not stop them from making a bigger move at linebacker before the trade deadline. However, with the injury happening on Sunday, this is a quick pivot. Lions Add Depth at LB Before Week 9 Pappoe is a fifth-round pick by the Arizona Cardinals . Pappoe has been a notable special teams contributor for his first three NFL seasons. Despite just two starts in three seasons, he was active for every game. Pappoe has 960 career special teams snaps, with 16 coming this season. He also has 341 snaps in his NFL career. He played 114 snaps as a rookie, 131 the following season, and then only 96 in 2025. He did not see the field on defense in 2026. He started the year on the Tennessee Titans . He started on their practice squad, but was also called up for special teams duties in Week 2. The Titans released him on October 6. After being a free agent for nearly a month, he finally caught on with the Lions’ practice squad. His experience on special teams will make him a competitive option for Bachie as the sixth linebacker. The Lions take on the Miami Dolphins in Week 9. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Lions Sign Ex-Cardinals Draft Pick After Jack Campbell Injury appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Ex-Giants QB Russell Wilson Interviewed for FBS Head Coaching Job
item.description: New York Giants QB Russell Wilson. Getty Former New York Giants quarterback Russell Wilson could be headed for a major career shift less than one year after the end of his NFL career. “Former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching job at NC State, ” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on Tuesday night. “Wilson, 38, joins Philip Rivers as former NC State and NFL quarterbacks who are now prominent candidates for the Wolfpack job. NC State fired Dave Doeren as head coach on Oct. 24. Wilson played at NC State from 2008 to 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin in 2011. After being taken by Seattle in the third round of the 2012 NFL draft, he went on to play 14 seasons in the NFL, leading the Seahawks to their first Super Bowl championship in the 2013 season.” Wilson, a 10-time NFL All-Pro, retired in June after spending one season with the Giants in 2025 and has been working for CBS Sports as an analyst this fall. “Interesting that Russell Wilson and Philip Rivers are contenders,” NFL reporter Ed Werder wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. Wilson spent his first 10 seasons with the Seattle Seahawks , where he won one Super Bowl and played in another before a blockbuster trade to the Broncos before the 2022 season. He lasted 2 seasons in Denver before spending one season each with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Giants . Broncos’ Wilson Trade One of NFL’s All-Time Worst Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox called the Broncos’ trade with the Seahawks for Wilson “Worst NFL Trade of the Last 10 Years” for the franchise. By releasing Wilson in April 2024, the Broncos were forced to take an NFL-record $85 million dead cap hit spread across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. “The Denver Broncos’ ill-fated 2022 trade for Russell Wilson has largely been overshadowed by the disastrous deal Cleveland made for Deshaun Watson in the same offseason,” Knox wrote. “However, that doesn’t mean that Denver’s deal was a good one. In fact, the Wilson trade might be considered the worst of the last decade if not for the Watson debacle. The Broncos coughed up two first-round picks, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick, quarterback Drew Lock , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and tight end Noah Fant to acquire Wilson and a fourth-round pick. The Broncos then signed Wilson to an extension worth $242.6 million over five years with $161 million guaranteed.” Russell Wilson, Sean Payton Butted Heads in 2023 The writing was on the wall for Wilson once Nathaniel Hackett was fired after one season as Denver’s head coach in 2022 and replaced with former New Orleans Saints head coach and Super Bowl champion Sean Payton. Wilson and Payton famously butted heads, but the bottom line was that Wilson went 11-19 over 2 seasons in Denver before he was released. Wilson and Payton famously butted heads, but the bottom line was that Wilson went 11-19 over 2 seasons in Denver before he was released. Wilson rejuvenated his career somewhat in 2024 with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a 1-year, $1.2 million contract. After missing the first 6 games of the season due to injury — Justin Fields started in his place — Wilson returned to go 6-5 for the Steelers, who made the AFC Playoffs before losing to the Baltimore Ravens in the AFC Wild Card Round, with Wilson going 20-of-29 passing for 270 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Wilson signed a 1-year, $10.5 million contract with the New York Giants on March 27 — just one month before they selected Ole Miss quarterback Jaxson Dart in the first round of the 2025 NFL draft . item.title: ‘I Need to Do Better,’ ‘Maybe I Should Chill’ — Caitlin Clark Makes Honest Admission About Major Source of Criticism
item.description: Caitlin Clark discusses trash talk, referees and the competitive habit she believes she needs to manage better. Caitlin Clark has never been shy about showing emotion on the court, but the Indiana Fever star says one part of her competitive reputation may be overstated. During Tuesday’s special episode of Kylie Kelce’s “Not Gonna Lie” podcast, she was asked about her on-court behavior, leading to a candid admission about one tendency she knows she needs to work on. Caitlin Clark Admits Referees Get More of Her Attention Than Opponents Kelce asked whether the former No. 1 pick was an underrated trash talker, and she disagreed . “See, people always think that I’m a trash talker. I don’t even think I really am,” Clark said. She explained that her exchanges with opponents are usually playful, recalling a moment against Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty during the 2025 season: “There was a clip that went viral last year when we played the Liberty and I made a 3 over Stewie. And me and Stewie just both started laughing, ’cause it was funny.” The Fever guard then brought up another part of her on-court behavior: “I don’t really trash talk like that, honestly. I mean, if somebody says something to me, I’ll probably go back. Honestly, the people I talk to the most is the refs, which I need to do better at. Maybe I should chill on that a little bit.” Kelce later asked if any particular player stood out as a trash talker. She said opponents rarely direct much trash talk her way. “People don’t really talk trash to me,” Clark said, drawing a “What a flex” from Kelce. The 2024 WNBA Rookie of the Year added that she enjoys those exchanges when they happen. “I want you to say something to me,” Clark said. “And I try to honestly do my best to just act like I can’t hear. I love that. I think that’s funny.” Her interactions with officials drew attention throughout the 2026 season, including an August technical foul that nearly resulted in a suspension. During Indiana’s 90-86 win over the Chicago Sky on Aug. 8, Natasha Cloud bumped Clark as she drove along the baseline. The Fever floor general passed the ball and went out of bounds, where her momentum carried her into an official. SEE ALSO: ‘A Little Silly In My Opinion’ — Caitlin Clark Reveals 1 Change She Would Make to WNBA Playoffs After Fever’s First-Round Exit The contact initially resulted in her eighth technical foul of the season. Fever coach Stephanie White also received one for arguing the call. Indiana appealed immediately, and the WNBA rescinded the technical, ESPN’s Kareem Copeland reported. The decision spared Clark a suspension that would have kept her out of the Fever’s Aug. 11 home game against the Liberty. It was the first time that season the Fever had successfully appealed a technical foul assessed to Clark. item.title: ‘I Really Hope He Doesn’t Get Fined For This’ — Packers Fans Beyond Amused as Jordan Love And His Wife Troll NFL Refs After Lions Controversy
item.description: ‘I Really Hope He Doesn’t Get Fined For This’ — NFL Fans Beyond Amused as Packers Star Jordan Love And His Wife Troll Refs After Lions Controversy Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love and his wife, Ronika Stone Love, found a hilarious way to express their frustration with NFL officiating this Halloween. The couple’s costume quickly went viral, with fans fully embracing their not-so-subtle dig at officials following Green Bay’s controversial loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 7. Love and Ronika dressed up as blind NFL referees, complete with the zebra-striped shirts, dark sunglasses, and white canes. Jordan Love and His Wife’s Halloween Costumes Get Fans Talking The joke went viral after Ronika posted a clip on TikTok captioned “I’m joking, I’m joking.” In the video , the couple can be seen blindly stumbling around, tapping their white canes, and launching yellow penalty flags into the air for no apparent reason. Fans quickly filled the comments section, with many finding the joke hilarious while others worried the quarterback could face a fine from the NFL. One fan joked, “You’re gonna get us fined.” Another supporter jokingly remarked, “Chill, Ronika, we play away this weekend, the refs might see this.” Others shared similar concerns, with one commenter saying, “I can smell the fine coming,” while another added, “I really hope he doesn’t get fined for this.” One fan even offered to cover the cost, saying , “I’ll pay the fine” Love’s wife also joined the fun in the comments, responding to the growing attention with a simple message intended to cover all bases: “We’re Footlocker employees.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Why the Halloween Costume Went Viral The couple’s costume was more than just a random Halloween gag, of course. It came after Green Bay suffered a frustrating 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 7, with several officiating decisions becoming a major talking point. Referee Alex Moore’s crew called eight penalties against the Packers for 81 yards, with some decisions drawing criticism from fans and analysts. The biggest talking point was the roughing-the-passer calls against defensive linemen Brenton Cox Jr. and Karl Brooks. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Brooks was flagged late in the fourth quarter after making contact with Jared Goff following an 18-yard completion. Tom Brady, in the FOX booth for the game, was clearly unhappy with the decision, saying, “That’s definitely not roughing the passer!” Former NFL Vice President of Officiating Dean Blandino also backed Brady’s criticism. Other calls against defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt for unnecessary roughness and an intentional grounding penalty against Love added to Green Bay’s frustration. The controversy continued to attract attention even after the game ended. item.title: Emiliano Martínez, Valentín Barco, Aarón Anselmino called up by Argentina
item.description: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez during the Premier League match between Everton and Chelsea at Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, United Kingdom, on October 17, 2026. (Photo by Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images There’s an international break after this weekend’s matches, but for a fair few Chelsea boys, there will be no rest. And among those set for national team duty are our trio or Argentinians. Trio? — you might ask. Who all could that be? After all, Enzo Fernández is gone. Alejandro Garnacho is gone. And Emi Martínez has a broken face. Who’s left? Valentín Barco. Sure. Get in the chopper! But joining Barco are indeed Martínez, and, in an even bigger surprise, Aarón Anselmino — man with no actual minutes of competitive senior football yet this season. Maybe Argentina just want their own Estêvão situation. Argentina are playing only a couple friendlies during this break, against Uruguay and Costa Rica, and manager Lionel Scaloni is using this opportunity to check out some fresh faces. Anselmino is one of two players called up with zero senior caps, and one of nine with less than five. (Barco himself is barely above that threshold at seven.) And Emi’s inclusion is hopefully a good sign that is recovery from the fractured jaw he suffered against Everton a few weeks ago is going well. Let’s see that mask! #SelecciónMayor Lista de convocados para los próximos amistosos 🇦🇷 📝 https://t.co/SqoaIewEQR pic.twitter.com/Kxysq82w1A — 🇦🇷 Selección Argentina ⭐⭐⭐ (@Argentina) November 3, 2026

item.title: Viola Station 107: The more things change
item.description: We’re sticking our necks out a bit with some of these takes. | Jacob King/PA Images via Getty Images So full disclosure: we recorded this before the Sassuolo game . And our collective emotional state was considerably lower. We were, in fact, struggling with our feelings. The podcast reflects that because, in hindsight, we were a little bit grim about Fiorentina’s prospects going forward. That’s apparent in pretty much everything we discussed. What did we discuss? Well, we ran through the recent history, picking our standouts (big dogs, boneheads, et cetera) before considering some tactical and statistical stuff which, in hindsight, probably doesn’t matter as much after Fiorentina got its wait a minute second? That can’t be right, can it? Second win of the season? Okay, yeah, maybe we weren’t entirely wrong in being ruffled. That Relegation Percent-O-Meter still resembles the Doomsday Clock. On the plus side, we got a wonderful McMike milestone, some unexpectedly terse Producer Mike analysis, and Tito completely failing to throw to an advertisement correctly. Thank you as always to ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Sport Social Podcast Network⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ for hosting us and to ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Windchime Weather⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ for the music. And as always, we hope you enjoy listening as much as we enjoyed making this. You could leave a rating and review if you want, but whatever.

item.title: Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nikita Kucherov wants out of the Tampa Bay Lightning , but he still can’t stop going all out for his team. Reports surfaced last Friday that the 33-year-old Kucherov had already asked the Lightning to move him. In the two games since, the two-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner has done nothing on the ice but rack up points. Against the Nashville Predators on Saturday on the road, Kucherov had a hand in three of his team’s goals, as he recorded a trio of assists, albeit in a 5-4 shootout loss to Steven Stamkos and company. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bolts returned to action on Tuesday, and Kucherov was clearly still feeling it, adding two more assists to his total in the 2026-27 NHL season. This time around, his effort did not go for naught, with the Lightning defeating the Detroit Red Wings, 4-2. Kucherov is in a contract year, which means he is on track to become a free agent next summer. However, he also clarified that his trade request is less about money and more about the perceived disrespect he feels from Tampa Bay over its “poor communication.” It remains to be seen how this saga between Kucherov and the Lightning will conclude, but what seems to be clear is that he is not shortchanging the only team he’s played for so far in his NHL career when it comes to his effort and production on the ice. Kucherov and the Lightning improved to 9-3-2 after the win against Detroit. Up next for them is a date with the visiting Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. item.title: Ex-Broncos QB Russell Wilson Interviewed for FBS Head Coaching Job
item.description: Denver Broncos head coach Russell Wilson. Getty Former Denver Broncos quarterback Russell Wilson could be headed for a major career shift less than one year after the end of his NFL career. “Former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching job at NC State, ” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on Tuesday night. “Wilson, 38, joins Philip Rivers as former NC State and NFL quarterbacks who are now prominent candidates for the Wolfpack job. NC State fired Dave Doeren as head coach on Oct. 24. Wilson played at NC State from 2008 to 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin in 2011. After being taken by Seattle in the third round of the 2012 NFL draft, he went on to play 14 seasons in the NFL, leading the Seahawks to their first Super Bowl championship in the 2013 season.” Wilson, a 10-time NFL All-Pro, retired in June and has been working for CBS Sports as an analyst this fall. “Interesting that Russell Wilson and Philip Rivers are contenders,” NFL reporter Ed Werder wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. Wilson spent his first 10 seasons with the Seattle Seahawks , where he won one Super Bowl and played in another before a blockbuster trade to the Broncos before the 2022 season. He lasted 2 seasons in Denver before spending one season each with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Giants . Broncos’ Wilson Trade One of NFL’s All-Time Worst Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox called the Broncos’ trade with the Seahawks for Wilson “Worst NFL Trade of the Last 10 Years” for the franchise. By releasing Wilson in April 2024, the Broncos were forced to take an NFL-record $85 million dead cap hit spread across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. “The Denver Broncos’ ill-fated 2022 trade for Russell Wilson has largely been overshadowed by the disastrous deal Cleveland made for Deshaun Watson in the same offseason,” Knox wrote. “However, that doesn’t mean that Denver’s deal was a good one. In fact, the Wilson trade might be considered the worst of the last decade if not for the Watson debacle. The Broncos coughed up two first-round picks, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick, quarterback Drew Lock , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and tight end Noah Fant to acquire Wilson and a fourth-round pick. The Broncos then signed Wilson to an extension worth $242.6 million over five years with $161 million guaranteed.” Russell Wilson, Sean Payton Butted Heads in 2023 The writing was on the wall for Wilson once Nathaniel Hackett was fired after one season as Denver’s head coach in 2022 and replaced with former New Orleans Saints head coach and Super Bowl champion Sean Payton. Wilson and Payton famously butted heads, but the bottom line was that Wilson went 11-19 over 2 seasons in Denver before he was released. Wilson rejuvenated his career somewhat in 2024 with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a 1-year, $1.2 million contract. Getty Former Denver Broncos quarterback Russell Wilson could be headed for a major career shift less than one year after the end of his NFL career. “Former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching job at NC State, ” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on Tuesday night. “Wilson, 38, joins Philip Rivers as former NC State and NFL quarterbacks who are now prominent candidates for the Wolfpack job. In fact, the Wilson trade might be considered the worst of the last decade if not for the Watson debacle. The Broncos coughed up two first-round picks, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick, quarterback Drew Lock , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and tight end Noah Fant to acquire Wilson and a fourth-round pick. The Broncos then signed Wilson to an extension worth $242.6 million over five years with $161 million guaranteed.” Russell Wilson, Sean Payton Butted Heads in 2023 The writing was on the wall for Wilson once Nathaniel Hackett was fired after one season as Denver’s head coach in 2022 and replaced with former New Orleans Saints head coach and Super Bowl champion Sean Payton. Wilson and Payton famously butted heads, but the bottom line was that Wilson went 11-19 over 2 seasons in Denver before he was released. Wilson rejuvenated his career somewhat in 2024 with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a 1-year, $1.2 million contract. After missing the first 6 games of the season due to injury — Justin Fields started in his place — Wilson returned to go 6-5 for the Steelers, who made the AFC Playoffs before losing to the Baltimore Ravens in the AFC Wild Card Round, with Wilson going 20-of-29 passing for 270 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Wilson signed a 1-year, $10.5 million contract with the New York Giants on March 27 — just one month before they selected Ole Miss quarterback Jaxson Dart in the first round of the 2025 NFL draft . item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
item.description: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe at the Estadio Metropolitano
item.content:encoded: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...

item.title: Raphinha underlines Barcelona’s class to give Aston Villa a reality check
item.description: This was a chastening night for Aston Villa, and a familiar one for Unai Emery in this corner of town. On a processional night at the Camp Nou Barcelona produced a performance of unhurried, high-grade incision, easing to a 3-0 Champions League victory that never really seemed to tip into an actual close-quarter contest before it was already gone. “There are a lot of things to learn today,” Emery said afterwards. “Overall we are competing fantastically in the Champions League; we have nine points. Today, we saw there is still more to do to get to this level. Even sometimes in this match we were close to achieving it. We had chances, but we must be ruthless in the final third. Three-nil maybe was more than we deserved.” Continue reading...
